repo_head_at_start: b12ef39 (main, up to date with origin/main; includes D-107 bearer-token fix and D-109 reproducer-persistence fix, both independently reviewed and merged: D-108 cybersecurity CLEARED, D-110 cybersecurity CLEARED, D-111 qa-engineer APPROVED)
objective: Sixth live attempt at the #50 D7 gate. All blockers found by runs 4/5 are fixed and merged. Drive one real mission through all nine steps against pktcfg, obtain both verdicts (VERIFIED and REJECTED) within a single mission (the literal reading of CEO doc section 3 / issue #50's acceptance criteria, confirmed by re-reading docs/09-company/01-vision-and-p0-cut.md section 3 and D-090's own design, which built exactly this shape and already had unit-test coverage for it -- this is the first LIVE, HTTP-driven confirmation of that shape), export and independently read back the evidence bundle, and confirm zero-stray teardown.

interpretation_note.question: Does '#50's acceptance criteria: both verdicts produced in that single run -- one Verified, one Rejected' require ONE mission producing both verdicts, or is it satisfied by two sibling missions within one rehearsal session (D-098/D-105's approach)?
interpretation_note.finding: docs/09-company/01-vision-and-p0-cut.md section 3 ('The minimum viable demo') describes ONE sequence run back to back on ONE target: step 7 says a second candidate 'goes through the identical pipeline' (implying the same mission's pipeline), and step 8 says the evidence bundle contains 'both diffs, both gate matrices, both verdicts' -- one bundle, both verdicts. D-090 (T-3, the operator-candidate endpoint) was explicitly built to support exactly this: 'A mission this endpoint already advanced to VERIFY can still accept a second operator-supplied candidate as long as no verification has run yet ... exactly the shape the D7 gate's acceptance criteria need,' and D-090's own test (test_operator_candidate_submission.py) already proved this end-to-end via the Django test client, but no prior LIVE rehearsal (D-084/D-085/D-098/D-105) had actually driven this shape through the real HTTP API against a real live-discovered finding -- each used sibling missions instead, likely because the reproducer-persistence gap made VERIFIED unreachable regardless of mission topology at the time.
interpretation_note.decision: Chose the more rigorous, literal reading: one mission, two operator-submitted candidates against the same live-discovered finding, both verified through real VERIFY jobs, both verdicts visible in one evidence bundle. Achieved and confirmed live this run (see mission d6897640 below).

blockers_found_this_run.title: SANDBOX_FUZZ_IMAGE in .env (both repo-root and apps/control-api/.env) pointed at a stale, no-longer-existent image digest
blockers_found_this_run.detail: First mission's FUZZ job failed: 'Unable to find image brahmadatta-fuzz-toolchain@sha256:e1183075... locally / pull access denied' -- the locally-built brahmadatta-fuzz-toolchain:local image's real digest (confirmed via docker image inspect) was sha256:65d33eef0279..., not the stale sha256:e1183075... value both .env files carried over from an earlier session's build. Not an application-code bug -- a plain environment-variable value drifted stale across sessions, exactly the kind of config-drift devops owns.
blockers_found_this_run.root_cause: A previous build-fuzz-image.sh run (or a manually retagged image) produced a different digest than what .env recorded; nothing re-synced the two automatically.
blockers_found_this_run.fix: Re-ran infrastructure/scripts/build-fuzz-image.sh to get the current, real digest (sha256:9c6c226453415ccd5efc617dcfd606b94cd0caa9c2029ffca565195a1dd4f347), updated SANDBOX_FUZZ_IMAGE in both .env and apps/control-api/.env to match, restarted fuzz-worker (bare-metal, reads env at start) to pick it up. Confirmed fixed live: the very next mission's FUZZ job succeeded (4400 executions, 1 unique crash, 0.3s).
blockers_found_this_run.authority: devops-engineer, plain infra/config value -- no application code touched.
blockers_found_this_run.cost_this_run: ~2 minutes; killed the first mission (0265f8a4), which was abandoned rather than retried (its FUZZ job had already exhausted its attempts and the mission had auto-transitioned to FAILED with teardown confirmed by the time the fix landed).

blockers_found_this_run.title: MODEL_ENDPOINT unset in .env, so PATCH_GENERATE's live-model call silently fell back to SMALL_MODEL_BASE_URL (http://model-host:11434, no /api suffix) instead of the documented default endpoint shape (http://127.0.0.1:11434/api) -- the model-host-auth sidecar's nginx proxy has no route at the bare host root, only under /api/*, so every live-model call 404'd
blockers_found_this_run.detail: Second mission's PATCH_GENERATE job (default, unrestricted worker, live-model path tried first per this task's own instruction) got PAST D-107/D-108's bearer-token fix cleanly -- no 401, confirming that fix live for a third time, independently, in this session -- and then failed with 'HTTP Error 404: Not Found'. Root-caused by reading gateway/ollama.py::_endpoint_url (urljoin(endpoint.rstrip('/') + '/', route.lstrip('/'))) against gateway/ollama.py::DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT ('http://127.0.0.1:11434/api') and patch_generate_executor.py::_build_live_backend (endpoint=settings.endpoint or DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT -- the 'or' never triggers because settings.endpoint is populated by the SMALL_MODEL_BASE_URL fallback, which is a bare host:port with no /api suffix): the resulting request URL was http://model-host:11434/chat, which model-host-auth's nginx (location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:11435; }) forwards to Ollama unchanged, and Ollama itself has no route at /chat, only /api/chat -- hence 404, from Ollama, after correctly clearing the auth gate.
blockers_found_this_run.root_cause: MODEL_ENDPOINT is documented in .env.example as 'the gateway's own endpoint variable ... Blank here falls back to SMALL_MODEL_BASE_URL' -- but SMALL_MODEL_BASE_URL's own documented value has never included the /api suffix DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT uses, so the fallback silently produces a different (and broken) endpoint shape than the coded default. A plain, pre-existing environment-variable configuration gap -- MODEL_ENDPOINT was simply never set to a working value in this .env, not an application-code defect (the code's own default, DEFAULT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT, is correct; it's just never reached once SMALL_MODEL_BASE_URL is non-empty).
blockers_found_this_run.fix: Set MODEL_ENDPOINT=http://model-host:11434/api explicitly in .env (the documented override variable, left blank by convention until this run), recreated the worker container to pick it up.
blockers_found_this_run.verification: Confirmed with a direct, manual POST /api/chat call from inside the worker container, using the real gateway code's endpoint-construction shape and the real bearer token: request now clears the model-host-auth sidecar (no 401, no 404) and reaches Ollama itself, which returned a real, structured Ollama-shaped error: HTTP 500, body {"error":"model requires more system memory (8.4 GiB) than is available (7.0 GiB)"}. This is the identical failure shape D-110's own independent cybersecurity review hit in its own sandbox (see D-110 in .project/decisions.md) -- a host memory-admission constraint on this specific Docker Desktop VM (allocated 7.65GiB; codellama:7b-instruct needs 8.4GiB to load), not a code or config defect. docker info confirms Total Memory: 7.653GiB; this Mac has 16GiB physical, so headroom exists to raise Docker Desktop's VM memory allocation, but doing so requires editing Docker Desktop's own settings-store.json and restarting the whole Docker Desktop application -- a machine-wide, unsupported-by-CLI change that would tear down every currently-running container on this host mid-rehearsal. Judged not worth the risk/time tradeoff against this run's ~75-minute budget, given cybersecurity's own independent review (D-110) already accepted the identical constraint as expected environmental variance rather than something to fix.
blockers_found_this_run.authority: devops-engineer for the MODEL_ENDPOINT fix (plain env value); the memory ceiling itself is a host-resourcing constraint, explicitly not chased further -- flagged, not fixed.
blockers_found_this_run.not_fixed: Docker Desktop's VM memory allocation (7.65GiB, host has 16GiB) -- raising it needs a Docker Desktop restart, out of scope for this run's risk budget. Recommend a deliberate, scheduled (not mid-rehearsal) bump to e.g. 10-12GiB before the next rehearsal or the actual finale run, if a live-model PATCH_GENERATE verdict is ever required rather than merely attempted.

live_model_attempt.outcome: Reached Ollama itself for the first time in this project's rehearsal history (past both the bearer-token gate, D-107/D-108, and the endpoint-path bug, blocker 2 above) -- blocked only by this host's Docker Desktop VM memory ceiling (7.65GiB allocated vs 8.4GiB the model needs to load), not by any code defect. Confirmed both via the live mission's real PATCH_GENERATE job (HTTP 404, before the endpoint fix) and via a manual, independent verification call (HTTP 500 with a real Ollama memory-admission error, after the endpoint fix). This is the deepest the live-model path has ever been proven to reach in this project's history.
live_model_attempt.fallback_used: Per this task's own pre-authorization ('falling back to the operator-supplied-candidate endpoint only for whichever verdict shape it doesn't reliably produce'): restricted the compose worker to --kinds BASELINE,CORRELATE,EXPORT,SANITIZER_BUILD,TEARDOWN,VERIFY (excluding PATCH_GENERATE) for the mission that actually produced the gate's two verdicts, so it parked cleanly in PATCH instead of auto-advancing to the dead-end HUMAN_REVIEW state on a live-model failure (the same devops-scoped topology control D-098/D-105 established). Reverted to the default (unrestricted) CONTROL_API_WORKER_CMD in .env after this run, matching D-098/D-105's own convention of not persisting a run-scoped workaround.

abandoned_missions_this_run.reason: First mission, created before blocker 1 (stale SANDBOX_FUZZ_IMAGE digest) was fixed. FUZZ job failed twice (docker image pull denied), mission auto-transitioned to FAILED with teardown confirmed by the orchestrator before the fix landed. Left as-is (FAILED, torn down) rather than retried -- a fresh mission was cheaper than trying to resurrect a terminal one.

Second mission, default unrestricted worker, used to genuinely try the live-model PATCH_GENERATE path first per this task's own instruction. BASELINE/FUZZ/CORRELATE all succeeded live (8/8 ctest; 4979 executions, 1 unique crash). PATCH_GENERATE reached Ollama itself for the first time (past the bearer-token gate) but hit blocker 2 (missing /api suffix) as a 404, exhausted its single attempt (MAX_ATTEMPTS_BY_KIND[PATCH_GENERATE]==1), and the mission auto-transitioned to HUMAN_REVIEW -- a dead-end state (TRANSITIONS[HUMAN_REVIEW]==frozenset(), D-090's own documented design) that the operator-candidate endpoint explicitly refuses to accept a submission against (_ACCEPTING_STATES check, InvalidStateTransitionError). Left in HUMAN_REVIEW rather than resurrected -- this data point is itself valuable (it is what let blocker 2 be diagnosed) and a third, fresh mission was the correct next step per this project's own standing pattern (D-098/D-105) of restricting the worker's kinds once the live-model path has been genuinely tried and found not-yet-reliable, rather than looping on it.
